**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow the final checkout to release the pinned target**

When the documented release runs with `--sha 98a561a9...` from this final commit (or its protected-main merge), execution stops before preflight: `assertReleaseCheckout` compares that SHA to HEAD and permits only changes to `scripts/production-release.mjs` or `memory/`, but this commit also changes three identity docs and `scripts/__tests__/provider-rollback.test.mjs`. Consequently the new recovery policy cannot execute from the reviewed final checkout; either those known non-application paths must be allowed or the release target/checkpoint must be arranged so the checkout assertion passes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in 7d49563ec: the runbook now pins clean runner-only checkout 9fd718923895f331b505ea8850a0b525be4b8039 after protected-main inclusion, with application target 98a561a9446a1c51e627f6ad5a48737fe5122d85. Its only target-to-HEAD change is scripts/production-release.mjs, satisfying the existing guard. The final docs/test checkout is explicitly unsupported for this pinned target. The guard is not weakened.

Final arrangement: candidate 261bfdfbbdab0520b35725a72b776f160b608dd3 includes the runner, current main and reviewed dialog fix. It has its own full Build Image run35382946062. Production will run from a clean checkout of that exact SHA after protected-main incorporation, using verified recovery98a561a9. No older-target checkout exception is now needed. Actual261/recovery98 plan passes all113 migration ancestry and expanded-SQL checks.
